name: Drupal
description: Drupal is an open-source, API-first content management system for building structured, composable digital experiences across websites and channels.
best_for: Higher education, government, healthcare, nonprofit, and enterprise organizations that need an open-source, highly customizable CMS with no vendor lock-in.
cons: Drupal itself sells nothing and supports nothing directly — all commercial support, hosting, and implementation must be sourced from third-party certified partners or hosting companies, so there is no single official price list to budget against.

Security-advisory coverage for contributed, non-core modules is opt-in and conditional: the security team only covers stable releases of contributed projects whose maintainers applied for and were granted coverage, not every module automatically.

Drupal 10 reaches official end-of-life on December 9, 2026, after which no further security releases are issued for it, so sites still on Drupal 10 must budget an upgrade to a newer major version imminently.
features: Layout Builder for visual page composition
Multisite support for managing multiple sites from one installation
Taxonomy system for content organization and classification
Enterprise-grade security with no vendor lock-in
Drupal CMS distribution with guided setup for marketers and site builders
